tiers.K1: our net price to the distributor = list x (1 - our margin)
tiers.K3: our reference dealer price = K2 x DB x DLR
tiers.K5: a competitor's observed retail price (what KS publishes)

underidentification: One retail price cannot yield both the margin and the distributionstructure - two unknowns, one equation. Either the reader supplies a landedcost and we derive their margin, or they supply their margin and we derivethe cost. That is why DB and DLR are dials here.
correction: iam_ks_price_gap.csv carries isze_price_source = IE40_PR00, so its index is official genuine LIST against an aftermarket retail listing. It is not a margin comparison, and it was labelled as one.
The same gap reads very differently by tier: the document states all three indices side by side so a reader cannot take one for the truth.
caveats: KS is one UK source, fanned across 18 market rows. There is no market dimension in it; every market average from it is composition.
KS aftermarket is GBP ex-VAT converted at 1.17, a rate set 2026-05-01.
The bridge prices are a distributor list, not a market price, and sit in their own column.
